posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
I finally got to play sentinels with other people, and when trying to explain some things to them I had a few thoughts. They also inspired me to do some heavy duty looking into so I might be posting here a bit in the coming weeks if I find something interesting.

 

1st: Less likely now that I did a little research, but still possible. Mainstay and Medico's developing powers seems a tad bit random. Not only is there very little in the explanation of why they slowly developed powers, but the nature of them and where it all happened are a bit shadowy as well. Plus we don't know who else mught have been effected. We do know it happened in college, we do know that it happened some years before (Medico goes through med school which happens after the general college where he and mainstay were changed).... woah... let's say medico did 4 years pre-med while in college with Mainstay. Then 4 years med school, that means that before they met Idealist it is safe to say they were exposed for approx. 8 years. How old is Idealist when her developing powers and her scientist mother's crazy cause issues? 8 years old. Mainstay and Medico's known locations are Wintersburg Arizona and Pheonix Arizona, which are only a very few miles apart, so it is possible that the college is very close to Pheonix, where Idealist was born and her mother was a scientist working with energy related to Medico. So it is possible that whatever gave Medico and Mainstay powers could have also given Idealist her powers.

My oringal point? Mainstay, Medico and Idealist might have gained powers from one of those myterious crystals that we see in Tactics and that we know gave Cosmic and Infinitor powers. If the crystal were being experimented on by the college it would be possible that the radiation could be diluted so that the power's were gradual. Also, Medico and Cosmic do use the same color energy and Medico could be considered an energy construct. One big hole in the theory is that Medico and Mainstay are listed with "Nuclear Radiation" as a power source, while Idealist is Unknown. The wiki says Idealists flip side references Houe of M and reality shifting powers so it is still possible to some extent.

 

Tangent: I wonder if Idealist's mother is a villain? She's never named, which is suspicious. Knocking her thru the wall might not have killed her (especaly with a device meant to change reality to bring her dead husband back to life) but instead might have left her wheelchair bound (the lady from the Crackjaw Crew?) or something similiar.

 

2nd tangent: Glimpsed at the tactics bios for the citizens, a few might have gotten their powers in similiar ways maybe even from the same source, but something else caught my eye. Truth and Dare came from project Cocoon, but Visionary (AKA Dreamer) was supposedly the only successfully born super from that project. Also Truth and Dare are decades older than the Dreamer. Finally, we have no idea who or what is actually behind Coccoon. It was supposedly the U.S. Government, but they weren't greenlit by the gov't until well after Truth and Dare were born and escaped. Secretary of Defense Anthony Partin supposedly set up Coccoon according to Visionary's bio, but none of that should have happened yet in the Sentinels Timeline. Very Strange disconnect there

 

2nd: I was explaining how the cards show how poeple change, demonstrating by pulling setback and promo and expat and promo, I also on a whim pulled scholar's Don't Dismiss Anything. So we know that Expat's incap side shows her after being defeated by the Citizens of the Sun (the bloody symbol seems to clearly be the Citizen's emblem). We don't know why they left her alive, but it could have something to do with the Scholar and Setback since DDA shows Scholar with Expat a very short time later, importantly I think after it starts raining. Look at Setback's incap, raining in an alleyway. It is possible that these two scenes happen within the same couple of hours. We know Setback and Expat are a couple, but we don't know when that started, what if it started early, maybe one-sided on Setback's part. Expat confronts citizens within the city, Setback and the Scholar interrupt, saving her life, but she doesn't see it that way. Maybe she even knew she was about to die and welcomed it. Expat might have a bit of a deathwish/low self esteem issue going on, her mom is Dawn, easily one of the most powerful supers on the planet, expat's lack of power is thrown into her face (literally with a blast from mommy dearest) in response expat picks up guns and tackles major threats constantly, look at Wagermaster's card with expat "What if you did have power?" that seems to be in response to the perhpas lament that she does not have powers. Go back to that alleyway, Setback thinks he saved her, she disagrees, blows-up at him, tears him down, he's no hero, just a goof playing in spandex. He leaves, she breaks, scholar keeps her together while setback throws away his costume. Later they both recover, take back up their mantles, work together. He's determined to prove himself, to act as the shield as he wanted to, she sees the change. Sacrifices herself to save him, taking a rocket. Instead of being the first time, this is the second time he's let her down, failed her.

 

Plausible?

A few more things that I have thought of. Sorry about the text wall.

 

First: in the story war kickstarter we saw a picture (trying to post it in) ![](upload://4cSSRl4l2lrCgS5GitCuKjaprtp.jpeg)

 

Okay, way big but it should work. Anyways, this is a picture of the Atleantean font of power. Notice anything interesting? Like how we have an eyeball with tentacles and teeth? Similiar beings are seen on PW Adept and also in Infinitor's deck. None of them look quite the same though, but it gives somethings to work with. For example, combine this art with the Pillars of Hercules. The 1pillars are supposedly in Atlantis, but look at the art, a pure white field with a brown smudge in the distance, most likely the entrance as it is behind the heroes and baron blade who stand before the pillars. The art always reminds me of the Hyoerbolic Time Chamber from Dragonball Z, which was a pocket dimension. With this and creatures that claerly look extradimensional in orign we can draw the conclusion that Atlantis was somehow involved with extraplanar beings and powers. Possibly the Realm of Discord or something similiar.

 

Add to this Cap. Cosmic's card Wounding Buffer. The artwork shows Parse, a blue guy we've never seen, and a temple. The temple looks vaguely greek in design and features a painting of a red orb with tentaclesque lines rising up around it. It looks cultish and that design could easily stand for an eyeball with tentacles.

 

The Blue guy is slightly fascinating, he shoots energy beams from his eyes, but it is hard to tell exactly what is going on with them. He could possibly be a Darkseid pastische, which could mean he is connected to a cult and possbly to Atlantis, just that Atlantis fell centuries ago and this cult is the newest form of this ancient threat.

2nd: PW Fanatic's incap is fascinating, actually PW Fanatic is fascinating in general. Firstly. it shows a whole new enemy, looks like a vampire to me(there's actually two, one clearly visible and the other barey visible above th incap text). Then there is a cathedral in the background, up on a ledge where an indistinct cloaked figure is standing. Looks like a new environment, somewhere underground since she is slammig back against a stalactite. What's really interesting though is the color scheme, brown rock and sickly green light. Look at regular fantic's incap. She's stuck to a brown wall by flaming sticks and sickly green light is glowing beneath her. I always assumed that this was when Apostate had captured her, but the only Apostate card that shows them together is Fallen Angel, where it is likely the spot where he defeated her and she is not wearing her armor as she is on her incap, instead she's in a clothe robe, as though she's been stripped of her defenses, whcih would be a great allegory for when Apostate brings her low. Also, the flaming sticks don't make sense in this contest, but what if instead the incap shows a completely different encounter, perhaps an early run in with these vampires and then the sticks would be stakes and we could be dealing with a conflict between a brutal vamp hunter, perhaps one who pinned fanatic so she wouldn't get involved, maybe even sacrificed himself (or herself) to stop the vamp threat.

 

Something else fascintating about PW Fantatic and regular Fanatic? PW is clearly much older. Fanatic looks like she's 18 or so 22 or 23 at the oldest. She's skinny, her especially her arms and hips. PW Fanatic is much thicker, her arms are nearly twice their old size, her hips are bigger, her neck, her entire face is much older. She looks closer to 30 now. Redeemer Fanatic is harder to tell, the armor is much bulkier, but could easily be the mid-point between these two. I bring this up in connection to my previous theory because this could now be a situation of a returning enemy, something Fanatic thought defeated, that almost brought her down when she was younger and more zealous, that has come back to threaten people again, only this time it is worse.

 

Tangent: Could give us a reason for the priest, she interrogated him in connection to the vamps.

 

Quick points of Interest

While going through looking for pics of Fanatic I looked at Silver Shadow, it is probably the first gathering of the Prime Wardens, but Tempest already has his sword so it would seem to be after Tempest is a gladiator in the Bloodsworn Colesium(sp)

 

Looking at Apostate's deck I saw the Orb of Delirium, which has a similiar style and color to Dealines Ataxia Sphere. Both are also relics, so this is probably a very important connection.

 

Looking at the Red guy with Green hands I'm becoming convinced he is amphibius and therefore could be connected to Atlantis. I think the Alien on PW Tempest's Incap is another Maerynian turned evil, possibly after being Gene-bound by Voss but escaping.

 

The BLue bug on Parse's Quick Calculation is Korrupton, the Last Infektor, from the Enclave of the Endlings. the flavor text mentions it hunting Parse

 

Never saw this until recently, but Parse's card Between the Lines has some black birds near Akashbhuta. With recent speculations I'm wiling to bet that these birds are controlled by the Matriarch and that she is fighting with Parse and the Prime Wardens against Akashbhuta.

 

Fanatic's Holy Nova card has some interesting Flavor text I dont remember reading: "You can hide in the Sun 'til you see the Light." -Apostate, Mystery Comics #367. Could be a literal reference of Fanatic flying into the sun to hide from Apostate after he's tried converting her, or it could be a a reference to living on the surface. We've never been clear on where Apostate is most of the time, but it isn't unreasonable to think he is sequestered underground while Fanatic is "in the sun" hiding from her "true nature".

 

Kaagra has a guy called Orrim the Hive-minded, which is a guy and two mutant rat-pig things with green tentacles wrapped around all three. The tentacles have eyes and the flavor text reads: "Hello! We are normal beings with Skeletons, just like you! Let us share a welcome hug!" -The Hiveminded, Tome of the Bizarre #41. This seems to obviously happen before meeting this guy in the arena. The back art for the Realm of Discord has always featured a green tentacle with a simliar eye. These beings might b connected to the whole atlantis mess as well, or be a seperate less major threat.

 

Realm of discord back art also shows a figure holding up a glowing fist, never saw that until today.

Just had a crazy thought, which led to some interesting question.

 

What if Fanatic is the "child" in the center? I doubt it, but there are some things we don't know that are interesting.

 

For example: Why did Fanatic come back to life. She would believe the Hand of God, but God works mysteriously and usually thru a third party. We also have a second person we know who was killed and came back to life, Haka. Interestingly it is possible to draw a lot of comparisons between Fanatic's power and Haka's, most importantly that they are both fueled by tradition and belief. Haka in his Ancient Maori chants and practices, Fanatic thru Christianity. What if they can be traced back to an original source? What if Haka was a sort of first test, the next we know of being Fanatic.

 

It might be possible to say Fanatic's ressurection was a one-time thing, while we know Haka is effectively immortal (holy crap, Haka is a hero version of Vandal Savage, I just got that!). However, I point you to her armor. It is one of the only cards in the game that can bring a hero back after they've hit 0 or less hp. And we have good reason to suspect that the armor is not inately powerful. Look at her backstory, the armor and sword she found her not that special. However, one morning she awoke, supposedly after using her own blood to write runes on her sword, which had now become Absolution. Where did the Aegis come from? Her armor wasn't carved in runes, but her blood could easily have infused the armor over the course of a few battles, and would therefore come to represent her ability to heal and revive very quickly.

 

Actually, even the Monty Python easter egg comparing her to the black knight could be a clue. The black knight was being spoofed, but he was able to survive any wound dealt to him without dying of blood loss, essentially immortal.
